html:
Eusebio Francisco Kino was an Italian Jesuit priest, mapmaker and astronomer who founded missions among the O'odham peoples of the Pimería Alta, today's Sonora in Mexico and southern Arizona, from 1687 until his death in 1711.

Born in the Tyrol, he studied mathematics and astronomy in Germany, joined the Society of Jesus, and asked to go to China. He was sent to New Spain instead, arriving in 1681. After a failed mission in Baja California, he went north.

For 24 years he rode thousands of miles among the Akimel O'odham, Tohono O'odham and Sobaipuri, founding missions such as Dolores, Tumacácori and San Xavier del Bac near Tucson. He brought cattle, horses, wheat and fruit trees, the start of ranching in the region. His journeys to the mouth of the Colorado showed that California was a peninsula, not an island, and his maps were used for a century. He argued against sending mission converts to forced labour in the Spanish mines.
